transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-12
Time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Lydia Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Dana Ortiz (CTO - Emerald), Ravi Kumar (Platform Architect), Maya Lee (Security Lead)

Summary section (auto-gen, may be rough):
- High-level: POC to validate Private deployment and private networking for Emerald Health. Focus on VPC peering vs PrivateLink, ensuring data residency in AWS us-west-2, benchmarks for latency and throughput, and compliance needs (HIPAA/BAA).

Transcript:
00:00 Lydia: hey everyone thanks for joining, this is Lydia from Redwood, i think we have folks from emerald, can you do a quick roll?
00:05 Dana: yes hi im dana ortiz, cto at emerald health, we have ravi and maya with us. thanks for setting this up.
00:10 Lydia: awesome, yeah samir and i are here to scope the poc, especially around private networking and data residency. i know you sent over a couple of notes, ravi?
00:18 Ravi: yeah, i sent a short doc with our network ranges and high-level constraints. main thing: all PHI must stay in us-west-2, no public egress, we prefer PrivateLink if possible but open to peering if latency is better. also we have a transit gateway with on-prem connections.
00:34 Samir: ok good, that helps. quick clarifying q — is the POC going to be purely in your VPC or do you want redwood private in a customer-managed account?
00:42 Dana: ideally customer-managed, yes. we prefer a private deployment where control plane is internal and the inference nodes are in our VPC, or at least dedicated VPC peered with ours.
00:50 Lydia: got it. for our terminology, we have a few options: 1) Redwood Private deployed into your account (we can deploy a private control plane + inference nodes), 2) Dedicated with VPC peering to our managed infra, or 3) Hosted with PrivateLink endpoints. each has tradeoffs.
01:07 Maya: can you expand on tradeoffs? especially from an audit and encryption standpoint.
01:12 Samir: sure. with customer-deployed Private, keys never leave your KMS, we can ship connectors to integrate with your HSM/KMS. With Dedicated + peering, you'll still rely on our infra but traffic flows over VPC peering or PrivateLink; we encrypt in transit and at rest, but key management is Redwood-managed unless we enable customer KMS integration. The hosted + PrivateLink path is simplest operationally but means more managed components on our side.
01:33 Ravi: latency is a big concern. Our SLO is 200ms P95 for short chat completions (prompt ~512 tokens). Can you hit that in us-west-2 with your recommended topology?
01:42 Samir: we typically see 100-150ms P95 for dedicated deployments in the same AZ, but that depends on model, sequence length, and batching. For hosted via PrivateLink it can be low as well, but peering avoids extra hops. We'll run the POC benchmarks to validate.
01:56 Dana: for workload sizing — our expected steady-state is ~200 qps (requests per second) with spikes to 800 qps for short windows. Mix is roughly 70% chat generation, 30% embeddings. Average seq length ~256 tokens for generations, embedding payloads are small. Does that map to resource needs you can share?
02:14 Samir: yes — for 200 steady qps with that mix we typically recommend 4-6 GPU endpoints (A100 class or equivalent) for the POC, with autoscale for spikes. embeddings are cheaper, could be handled by smaller CPU/FPGA-backed nodes depending on model. We'll size the nodes in the benchmark phase.
02:29 Maya: and audit logging? we need full request logs, redaction controls, and retention settings. Also SOC2 + HIPAA controls.
02:37 Lydia: we do SOC2 currently and can provide the security pack. For HIPAA we support BAAs and have audit logs, access controls (RBAC + SSO/SAML), and KMS integrations. we'll share the SOC2 summary and a sample BAA.
02:49 Ravi: on network side, can we do PrivateLink with endpoint services in our account so traffic stays internal?
02:55 Samir: yes, AWS PrivateLink endpoint services are supported. The pattern is: Redwood exposes an endpoint service, you create an interface endpoint in your VPC, traffic stays on the AWS private network. However, PrivateLink has per-NIC bandwidth considerations and can add latency if cross-AZ. VPC peering or Transit Gateway with peering to our VPC can reduce latency for high-throughput workloads.
03:18 Lydia: also important — egress constraints: you mentioned no public egress. We can ensure no public internet egress from inference nodes and restrict to your CIDRs for logging/observability. If you require no third-party data crossing region, we can pin nodes to us-west-2 and disable any cross-region replication.
03:35 Dana: excellent. For success criteria, we proposed: 1) latency P95 < 200ms for chat (512 tokens), 2) throughput sustaining 600 qps for 5-minute window with <5% error, 3) embeddings throughput 300 qps at cost below $X (we'll calibrate), 4) data residency: no data leaves us-west-2 and PHI encryption under our KMS. Does that look workable?
04:00 Samir: those are reasonable as POC success rules. We'll map them to runnable benchmarks. For the cost target, we'll need your expected token volumes to estimate.
04:09 Dana: initial pilot estimates: 50M tokens/month.
04:12 Samir: ok good — we'll model cost in the follow-up.
04:16 Ravi: any network requirements for CIDR overlap? we use 10.0.0.0/16 and have multiple subnets; we can create dedicated subnet for endpoints.
04:26 Samir: good, please share exact CIDR blocks. If there's overlap we can recommend AWS PrivateLink to avoid routes.
04:34 Maya: one more — audit and telemetry. We need to push logs to our SIEM (Splunk). Is there a straightforward way?
04:41 Lydia: yes we support pushing logs to your S3 in-region or via Kinesis/Firehose to Splunk; we can also share structured traces and token-level cost breakdowns. We'll document log formats in the security pack.
04:55 Dana: timeline — we want a 3-week POC followed by decision. Week 1: infra + network setup, Week 2: benchmark runs, Week 3: analysis and joint review. Is that realistic?
05:06 Samir: yes that's realistic if we have the network details and test data by the end of next week. We can parallelize infra setup and small-scale tests while waiting for bigger data.
05:16 Lydia: ok so immediate deliverables from redwood: security pack, sample deployment topology, benchmark harness. From emerald: CIDRs, dataset sample, and compliance checklist.
05:25 Ravi: about metrics collection — we need P95, P99, median latencies, error rates, and per-route token counts.
05:33 Samir: we'll expose those in the console and can export CSVs. For the POC we'll run a benchmark script (we'll share link) that hits the endpoints with realistic sequences; we'll include cold-start scenarios, KV cache warmup and batching behavior.
05:48 Maya: a question on keys: for the private deployment will the encryption keys be in our KMS with key policies blocking redwood access?
05:55 Samir: yes if you host KMS in your account and give limited IAM to the instances, that keeps keys under your control. We'll need temporary permissions for operator tooling during deploy but we can minimize scope.
06:07 Lydia: small note: sometimes automatic transcripts mess up product names — we call our product Redwood Private / Redwood Dedicated etc, but you'll see typos in the transcript, apologies in advance.
06:15 Dana: ha, no worries.
06:18 (brief cross talk)
06:25 Lydia: ok last section on bench specifics — Samir what will you measure?
06:29 Samir: we'll measure cold and steady-state latency, token throughput, concurrency scaling, and variance across AZs. We'll run models representative of your usage — probably a 13B open model for chat and a smaller embed model. For embedding throughput we'll test batch sizes of 16 and 64. We'll also measure cost per 1M tokens and memory footprint.
06:49 Ravi: curious about model quantization — do you support int8 or bf16 optimizations?
06:52 Samir: yes our runtime supports quantized paths (int8) for some model families which reduces memory and cost; we can include quantized variants in the benchmark.
06:59 Maya: any red flags on compliance? we need to ensure logs and telemetry are stored in-region and we can get an attestation for BAA controls.
07:07 Lydia: we'll provide the SOC2 report, and our legal/ops team can provide a BAA template. We'll flag which controls map to your HIPAA checklist.
07:16 Dana: perfect. ok wrapping — quick recap and owners?
07:20 Lydia: recap: Redwood to share security pack and topology + benchmark harness, SE runs bench, customer shares CIDRs and sample data, schedule network design and bench review. Agreed timeline: 3-week POC starting as soon as infra details provided.
07:35 Ravi: i'll send the CIDRs and the initial dataset by thursday (2027-09-15).
07:40 Maya: i'll send the compliance checklist and point contacts.
07:43 Lydia: great. we'll follow up with calendar invites for the network design sync and a benchmark kickoff.
07:49 Dana: thanks everyone, this was helpful.
07:52 Lydia: thanks, bye.
